article_content: 'Orange Is the New Black' actress Diane Guerrero broke down as she recounted the heart-wrenching day she arrived home from school, at age 14, to discover her parents had been deported to Colombia. Speaking to CNN on Monday, the 28-year-old actress recalled how she had returned to her Boston home after a day at school, excited to tell her family about being picked for a play. 'I got home and their cars were there and dinner was started and the lights were on, but I couldn't find them,' she told New Day. 'I broke down. I remember I hid under the bed because I was afraid somebody would come for me.' Scroll down for video Struggle: Diane Guerrero, an actress in 'Orange Is the New Black', broke down during an interview with CNN on Monday as she recalled how her parents were deported to Colombia from Boston when she was 14. Left behind: The 28-year-old sobbed as she said how her parents missed out on her growing up. Guerrero, who was born in New Jersey and grew up in Boston, spoke to CNN two days after writing an op-ed for the 'Los Angeles Times' calling for immigration reform so families don't get separated. After she arrived home to an empty house, no government official contacted her to tell her where her parents were, she said. 'No one checked to see if I had a place to live or food to eat, and at 14, I found myself basically on my own,' she wrote. Instead, neighbors told her what had happened and waited with her until her father was able to call from the detention center, she told CNN. Her parents were being held separately, she said, and her older brother, who had a young daughter at the time, had also been taken in by authorities. Alone at 14, she relied on the kindness of other families to take her in, allowing her to attend a performing arts school and eventually go to college. Despite having places to stay and working a variety of jobs to do her best to support herself, she feared it could be taken from her at any point, she wrote in the 'LA Times'. Painful past: Guerrero, pictured left as a child, said her father, right, and mother moved to the U.S. during a time of instability in Colombia and struggled to get properly documented. She now sees them once a year. 'I had a rocky existence,' she explained. 'I was always insecure about being a nuisance and losing my invitation to stay.' Her parents missed her recitals, her prom and her graduations from high school and college, she said. Despite the hurdles, she has achieved a successful acting career. She plays Maritza Ramos in 'Orange Is the New Black' and the role of Lina in CW's new show, 'Jane the Virgin'. She travels to see her family in Colombia once a year, she said - but their relationship has suffered. 'We've been separated for so long, I feel like sometimes we don't know each other,' she said, as she became emotional. 'I've grown up without them. There are things about them that I don't recognize. 'It hurts. I love them so much. I know that I've been by myself, but I feel like they have lived a very lonely existence themselves.' In her op-ed, she explained that her parents had moved to the U.S. during a time of 'great instability' in Colombia and had tried for years to get properly documented 'to no avail'. Battle: Despite her struggles, she went on to graduate college and now plays Maritza Ramos in OITNB (left) Looking forward: Guerrero, pictured with her boyfriend Joseph, is now calling for immigration reform. Still, she considers herself lucky, she said. Her brother's daughter was raised in a single-parent household after he was taken away - and she is now serving time in jail. 'I don't believe her life would have turned out this way if her father and my parents had been here to guide and support her,' she wrote in her op-ed. Guerrero, a U.S. citizen who volunteers at the nonprofit Immigrant Legal Resource Center, is now calling on the Obama administration to change policies to ensure families are not separated. 'I realize the issues are complicated,' she wrote. 'But it's not just in the interest of immigrants to fix the system: It's in the interest of all Americans. 'Children who grow up separated from their families often end up in foster care, or worse, in the juvenile justice system despite having parents who love them and would like to be able to care for them. 'I don't believe it reflects our values as a country to separate children and parents in this way.' See below for video

article_content: Mitt Romney commented that former President Bill Clinton 'embarrassed the nation' due to the Monica Lewinsky scandal. However, Romney doubts this will negatively impact Hillary Clinton's potential presidential campaign. Speaking on NBC's 'Meet The Press,' Romney stated that Hillary Clinton should be evaluated based on her own political career. He suggested that Bill Clinton's past actions would likely not be a central issue in the upcoming election. Yahoo News reported that Romney, the former governor of Massachusetts and 2012 Republican presidential nominee, addressed questions about President Clinton amidst renewed Republican discussions about Clinton's time in office. Romney described Bill Clinton's behavior during the Monica Lewinsky affair as 'embarrassing' for the United States on the global stage. He elaborated, saying Clinton 'breached his responsibility as an adult and a leader,' calling it 'very unfortunate.' Nevertheless, Romney clarified that Hillary Clinton should not be held accountable for her husband's actions. He emphasized her own 'record' and 'vision' for the country, anticipating these would be the focus of the 2016 campaign debates. article_content: Harry Reems, whose actual name was Herbert Streicher, the actor who became famous for his part as Dr. Young in the groundbreaking 1972 adult movie 'Deep Throat', passed away on Tuesday.  A representative from a hospital in Salt Lake City confirmed his death, stating he was 65 years old. Reems, a significant figure in adult films during the 1970s and 1980s, was described by fellow actor Ron Jeremy as a trailblazer. Jeremy highlighted Reems' fight for First Amendment rights, which he said helped pave the way for the adult film industry to gain wider acceptance. Jill Atwood, speaking for George E. Wahlen VA Medical Center in Salt Lake City, cited privacy concerns when declining to reveal the cause of death. Reems achieved stardom in 1972 when he was unexpectedly cast in 'Deep Throat'.  Originally an extra, he stepped into a main role when the actor slated for Dr. Young didn't appear. This promotion led to a memorable scene with the film's star, Linda Lovelace.  Despite the movie's modest $25,000 budget, of which Reems received only a small portion, the ensuing controversy and legal battles surrounding 'Deep Throat' catapulted him to fame in the 1970s adult film scene. Ron Jeremy emphasized Reems' foundational role, calling him 'the original' alongside John Holmes as the biggest names of their time. Larry Flynt, publisher of Hustler magazine, via his representative, stated that Harry Reems is universally recognized by anyone who has watched a pornographic film, describing him as an 'icon' from the industry's beginnings.  'Deep Throat' became a massive financial success, earning hundreds of millions, partly due to the extensive publicity from obscenity charges and the prosecution of Reems, which drew global attention. Although his obscenity conviction was later overturned, the legal fight became a significant First Amendment issue for some in Hollywood. Paul Fishbein, founder of AVN (Adult Video News), noted that the 'Deep Throat' controversy became a 'cause celebre'. Fishbein, now president of X3Sixty Network, pointed out that Reems became the public face of '70s obscenity due to his 'Deep Throat' fame.  His indictment was a major event.  Support for Reems' defense came from major Hollywood figures like Jack Nicholson and Warren Beatty, according to Jeremy, further cementing his status as a pioneer. Following 'Deep Throat', Reems starred in another notable adult film, 'Devil in Miss Jones' (1973).  His Internet Movie Database page lists 139 acting credits between 1970 and 1986, after which he retired from the industry.  Despite early aspirations for mainstream acting, his association with pornography hindered this ambition. He was initially chosen for the role of Coach Calhoun in the hit 1978 musical 'Grease', but was ultimately replaced by Sid Caesar. Jeremy fondly recalled his friendship with Reems in the 1980s, mentioning their time at Bernards, a New York bar popular with both Broadway and adult film actors.  He recounted lighthearted anecdotes about picking up women and sharing personal moments.  They frequently worked together and even participated in group scenes on set.  Jeremy described them as 'Jewish boys with big mustaches' who enjoyed dialogue-driven roles. Reems left the adult film industry in 1987 and relocated to Utah, where he reportedly 'found Jesus and decided to go Mormon'. Jeremy mentioned Reems expressed relief at leaving the porn industry behind. Reems transitioned to a career in real estate in Utah, initially using his birth name, Herbert Streicher. However, he later capitalized on his fame as Harry Reems to boost his real estate business, which Jeremy indicated was successful.  Jeremy mentioned Reems' death wasn't unexpected due to his declining health.  A memorial for Reems is planned by friends after a performance of the play 'Deep Throat Sex Scandal' at the Zephyr Theatre in West Hollywood on Saturday. CNN's Abbey Goodman and Jim Kavanagh contributed to the original report.

article_content: The Rolling Stones have released "Doom and Gloom," their first new song in seven years, effectively merging their classic sound with contemporary elements. Mick Jagger's lyrics touch on themes of class disparity and oil fracking, set against a backdrop of a Keith Richards guitar riff reminiscent of "Sticky Fingers." Charlie Watts' drumming provides a steady, powerful rhythm. Produced by Don Was and recorded in Paris earlier this year, "Doom and Gloom" is featured on the Stones' upcoming "GRRR! Greatest Hits" compilation, scheduled for release on November 13. This 50th-anniversary collection also includes another new track, "One More Shot," alongside iconic hits such as "Gimme Shelter," "(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction," "Jumpin' Jack Flash," "Start Me Up," and "Street Fighting Man." The release of "Doom and Gloom" has coincided with discussions about potential tour dates.  Rumors suggest possible performances in London and at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn before year's end, with touring saxophonist Bobby Keys hinting at additional concerts afterward. Furthermore, "Crossfire Hurricane," a new documentary chronicling the band's extensive career, is set to premiere on HBO on November 15. See the original article at Rolling Stone.

Jang Do-yeon then asked Suzy if she also focused on such details. Suzy confirmed she does, especially for continuity in 'Doona!', where her character often wears revealing outfits at home. She recounted a funny incident where, after overeating, she felt she had a slight tummy during shooting. Fortunately, the scene involved her character eating seaweed soup. Suzy explained that she used the soup-eating scene to her advantage, joking that her character's fuller belly after soup was intentional for continuity. Jang Do-yeon playfully added that seaweed can cause bloating, further supporting Suzy's lighthearted explanation. Suzy even shared that she had mentioned her "belly issue" to the director, who was initially surprised but then amused by her continuity "plan." 'Doona!' is a Netflix series featuring Suzy and Yang Se-jong, telling the story of a college student, Won-jun, and his unexpected cohabitation with Doona, a former K-pop idol, as they both start new life chapters. Suzy's frankness about a common concern highlights that even celebrities manage everyday issues and use clever on-set tactics to maintain seamless performances, contributing to the magic of storytelling on screen.

article_content: An investigation by an animal charity has uncovered that a subsidiary of the chocolate manufacturer Mars, known as Royal Canin, sponsored bear-baiting contests in Ukraine. Video footage captured by activists shows tape marked with the Royal Canin brand being used at a competition held earlier this year near Vinnytsia, in Ukraine. Royal Canin, a French pet food company acquired by Mars approximately ten years ago, stated they were 'horrified' upon learning about their sponsorship of the brutal event. The footage, released by the international animal welfare organization Four Paws, depicts a staged event in a wooded area. In this event, several dogs are unleashed upon a chained brown bear while a small group of men watches. The bear's claws have been removed, and its movements are restricted by men pulling on its chain. This prevents the bear from effectively defending itself against the dogs, which continuously attack and harass it. The video shows the distressed bear foaming at the mouth from exhaustion and fear. A table in the footage displays Royal Canin-branded trophies intended for the owners of the most aggressive dogs in the competition. Royal Canin, which produces pet food for cats and dogs, uses the slogan 'respecting the animal nature of dogs and cats'. However, Four Paws' evidence is likely to shock animal welfare advocates. The charity claims to possess evidence that Royal Canin has sponsored multiple bear-baiting contests. Four Paws reported that the event took place near Vinnytsia in central Ukraine earlier this year. Brown bears are legally protected in Ukraine but often suffer from mistreatment. Dr. Amir Khalil, a veterinarian and project leader at Four Paws, questioned Royal Canin's stated commitment to animal welfare in an interview with The Observer. He stated, 'By sponsoring bear-baiting, Royal Canin is devaluing wild animals like brown bears.' Four Paws has an agreement with the Ukrainian government to combat bear baiting. Despite this, these contests are estimated to occur four to six times annually. Although legally protected, brown bears in Ukraine have long been subjected to cruelty, often forced to perform in zoos and circuses. According to Four Paws, there are an estimated 15 to 20 bears used for baiting in Ukraine. These bears endure harsh conditions, kept in small cages most of the time and released only for training or attacks by dogs. A spokesperson for Four Paws described their lives as 'cruel', stating they are kept in 'tiny cages with nothing but a concrete floor' and often given insufficient food and water to weaken them against the dogs. Most baiting bears, whether from zoos, circuses, or the wild, are taken from their mothers when very young and undergo claw removal. The company stated that sponsoring the event was 'not consistent with Royal Canin's animal welfare policy, our pet-first philosophy or our vision'. Royal Canin said that after Four Paws informed them of the 'humbling' incident in May, they immediately stopped sponsoring bear-baiting contests. MailOnline contacted Mars UK for comment but was awaiting a response at the time of reporting.

article_content: Following a horrific car accident that resulted in the deaths of three individuals, Nei Lima Da Costa has admitted guilt to seven charges. The incident occurred when a Melbourne resident tragically witnessed her husband being struck and propelled 50 meters by a driver under the influence of drugs and exceeding the speed limit, as they were walking home from their wedding anniversary celebration. Nei Lima Da Costa was driving at approximately 120 kilometers per hour when he fatally struck Anthony Parsons at an intersection in Melbourne. Subsequently, his vehicle collided with another car, resulting in the deaths of Savvas and Ismini Menelaou, a married couple. Lima Da Costa, aged 30, has entered a guilty plea to seven charges, including dangerous driving causing fatality, negligent infliction of serious harm, and reckless endangerment. Sue Parsons, the widow of Mr. Parsons, expressed that Lima Da Costa's actions had robbed her of her 'soul mate, confidant, and best friend'. She was merely meters behind her 45-year-old husband when he was hit on January 12, as they were returning home after commemorating their 10th wedding anniversary. In a victim impact statement presented to the Victorian Supreme Court on Tuesday, she recounted, 'Words cannot express the horror of witnessing my husband being killed before my very eyes.' The force of the impact was so severe that it fractured every bone in Mr. Parsons' body, severed his arm, and propelled him 52 meters. Lima Da Costa, a citizen of Brazil, emerged from the wreckage of his car with only a broken collarbone. Blood tests confirmed the presence of methamphetamine, commonly known as ice, in his system. Mrs. Parsons recounted her frantic search immediately after the accident, stating, 'I was repeatedly asking people, 'Where is my husband? Where is my husband?''. She described discovering his severely injured body in a state of shock and desperately attempting to revive him. 'I kept gently tapping his arm, urging him to wake up,' she explained. 'I continuously said, 'Come on honey, wake up and talk to me,' but he remained unresponsive.' Prosecutor Andrew Tinney SC stated that Lima Da Costa was traveling 40 kilometers per hour above the speed limit when he disregarded a red traffic signal, initially hitting Mr. Parsons before crashing into a Ford sedan carrying Savvas Menelaou, 67, and Ismini Menelaou, 59, both of whom died at the scene. Their son, Menelaos Menelaou, the driver of the sedan, sustained life-threatening injuries. Another elderly couple who were passengers in the sedan also suffered significant injuries. Mr. Tinney mentioned that witnesses described seeing a 'white blur' as Lima Da Costa's car swerved through traffic and ignored red lights while traveling from Crown Casino in Melbourne's central business district to the crash site in Oakleigh. His plea hearing is ongoing. Reports indicate Lima Da Costa disregarded red lights on his route from Crown Casino prior to the collision in Oakleigh.

article_content: Ayan Hadi, the wife of convicted terrorist Richard Dart, received a 12-month suspended sentence at the Old Bailey for failing to provide information about his terrorist plot. Hadi, 31, residing in Acton, West London, admitted to not informing authorities about her husband, Richard Dart's, plan to travel to Pakistan for combat training, which had the potential to lead to acts of terrorism. She pleaded guilty at the Old Bailey to withholding information she knew could assist in her husband's apprehension, prosecution, or conviction for terrorism. Judge Sweeney stated during sentencing that 'justice could be tempered by mercy', especially in cases involving vulnerable individuals or those in relationships with a defendant. The court was informed that Hadi had suffered an abusive first marriage, felt isolated, and desired a stable family life. Her sentence comprised a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for two years, along with a two-year supervision order and a 10-year notification requirement to inform authorities of her whereabouts. Richard Dart had previously been jailed for six years in April, alongside two co-conspirators, Jahangir Alom and Imran Mahmood, for engaging in conduct in preparation for acts of terrorism. Judge Sweeney noted that Hadi had 'an element of choice' in her decision not to alert authorities after Dart revealed his intentions in November 2011. He also acknowledged that her experience with a 'clearly abusive' first husband had 'coloured in part' her reaction to the information Dart shared. Dart placed her in a 'difficult position', forcing her to choose between her love for him and her duty to inform the authorities. The judge recognized Hadi's good character and that neither she nor her family had demonstrated Jihadist sympathies. Hadi and Dart met online in August 2011 and married a month later. She claimed she was unaware of his extremist views until she watched a BBC documentary by his step-brother, Robb Leech, titled 'My Brother The Islamist'. The judge stated that Hadi had demonstrated 'remorse for her behaviour' and that this experience had made her aware of responsibilities she 'should have been aware of in the first place'. Imran Mahmood received a sentence of nine years and nine months, while Jahangir Alom was jailed for four years and six months. At their sentencing, the judge described all three as 'committed fundamentalists' who were prepared to kill. Dart and Alom traveled to Pakistan seeking terrorist training and received guidance from Mahmood, who had previously visited the country. Dart also discussed bomb-making with Mahmood and mentioned targeting Royal Wootton Bassett, a town that became a focal point for the repatriation of UK soldiers from Afghanistan. Dart, who changed his name to Salahuddin al-Britani, became involved in extremism after moving to East London and associating with radical Muslim preacher Anjem Choudary. Emails between Hadi and Dart indicated that she 'endorsed his security conscious approach'. The judge noted that 'it was equally clear that Dart made his terrorist intentions plain'. Mozammel Hossain, defending Hadi, described her as a decent woman, now with a young child, who married Dart without knowing 'the type of man that he was'. He depicted her as a woman desiring a warm, loving home life but who was 'quite weak willed' and suffering from a post-natal condition. Hossain added that she did not 'condone or support anything that her husband stood for' and that there was 'no evidence in this case that this lady held any radical or extremist views'. He argued that her actions were driven by her 'desire to keep in touch with her husband'. Dart also discussed bomb-making and Wootton Bassett as a potential target. Police discovered fragments of text on his laptop revealing 'silent conversations' used to evade surveillance, mistakenly believing deleted text would be unrecoverable. Forensic experts recovered fragments which showed Mahmood referencing Wootton Bassett and suggesting to 'deal with a few MI5 MI6 heads'. The trio were apprehended in a large surveillance operation by Scotland Yard and MI5 after attempting to train with Al Qaeda in Pakistan. Judge Simon stated that the trio held ‘radical Islamist beliefs’ and had ‘shown yourselves to be committed to acts of terrorism’. Mahmood and Dart received extended sentences, meaning they would serve two-thirds of their prison terms and spend five years on license. The judge said they were all 'committed fundamentalists' prepared to kill and that neither Dart nor Mahmood had ruled out an attack in the United Kingdom, with Mahmood considering acquiring a bomb. Dart had made appearances on YouTube and BBC TV discussing his faith and views, and attended anti-British protests. Counter-terrorism teams also believed the pair used mobile phones to communicate discreetly while walking in public. Judge Simon described the men as ‘dangerous’ and capable of killing. Anjem Choudary defended Dart, claiming he was jailed for a ‘thought crime’ and had ‘committed no sin and harmed nobody’, asserting ‘Jihad training’ is a duty for Muslim men. Dart became involved in extremism after moving to East London and associating with Choudary. The cleric appeared with Dart in the BBC film 'My Brother The Islamist'. In the documentary, Dart questioned 'misconceptions about Al Qaeda' and protested at a homecoming for soldiers. Met Deputy Assistant Commissioner Stuart Osborne described the case as ‘a classic example of how terrorists live in our midst’. Dart and Mahmood were both born in the UK, while Alom was born in Bangladesh but is a British citizen.

Hiriyyootni sadan hojii too'annaa guddaa Scotland Yard fi MI5n raawwataniin qabamaniiru erga Al Qaeda Paakistaan keessatti leenji'uuf yaalii godhanii booda. Abbaan Murtii Simon akka ibsanitti hiriyyootni sadan 'yaada Islaamaa cimaa' qabu akkasumas 'gocha shororkaa raawwachuuf akka of kennan' agarsiisaniiru. article_content: A 17-year-old girl, Chloe Wilkes, who left school last year, was found unresponsive at her home in Singleton, Kent. She passed away later the same day in hospital. Her father has been charged in court with manslaughter following Chloe's death after she took MDMA at home. Jason Wilkes, 44, is also charged with conspiracy to supply the illegal drug. Chloe Wilkes was discovered unresponsive at her semi-detached house in Ashford, Kent, on July 27. She was transported to William Harvey Hospital but was pronounced dead later that day. Jason Wilkes appeared before magistrates in Folkestone two days later and was remanded in custody to appear at Canterbury Crown Court on August 18. Teachers and friends have paid tribute to the 'sweet' teenager on a Facebook memorial page. Jon Whitcombe, headmaster of The North School in Ashford, where Chloe was previously a student, expressed condolences, saying, 'These are desperately sad circumstances, and our thoughts are with her family and friends during this very difficult time.' Chloe's friend, Tiffany King, created a Facebook page titled 'Chloe Wilkes - Little Angel Who's Now In Good Hands' in her memory. On this page, she wrote of her memories and expressed her grief. Other friends, including Luke Payne and Hayley Anne Powell, also shared their heartfelt messages of remembrance and love for Chloe. Rhiannon Leah Hamilton wrote about the profound impact of Chloe's passing and the deep sense of loss felt by her friends. Group members have been raising money for Chloe's family by selling candles and collecting donations. An inquest into Chloe's death was opened in Folkestone, Kent, and has been adjourned to a future date. Chloe was taken to William Harvey Hospital in Ashford, Kent, but unfortunately died on the same day. Comments are not currently being accepted on this article.

article_content: JAKARTA: India has inaugurated a five-day Millets Festival in Jakarta, Indonesia, to increase awareness of millets as a sustainable and farmer-friendly food option. The festival also aims to establish a market for millet-based products within the ten-member ASEAN bloc. The Indian Mission to ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) and the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare are jointly hosting the 'ASEAN-India Millets Festival', which began on November 22. A central feature of the festival is a Millet-focused exhibition showcasing Millet-based Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), start-ups, and Indian chefs. 'During the ASEAN-India summit on September 7, which the Prime Minister (Narendra Modi) attended, food security was highlighted in one of the joint statements,' stated Jayant Khobragade, India's Ambassador to ASEAN. He added, 'Within two months, we are holding this Millet Festival, which also addresses food security. This demonstrates the effective collaboration within our comprehensive strategic partnership.' Khobragade emphasized millets as crucial for ensuring food security and noted its alignment with the broader ASEAN-India relationship. 'There is significant interest in millets. This festival has attracted participants from ASEAN member states, as well as Indian farmers and industrialists,' he mentioned. He further stressed the importance of millets in tackling global hunger and nutritional deficiencies. Arief Prasetyo Adi, Head of Indonesia's National Food Agency (Badan Pangan Nasional (BPN)), highlighted millets as a sustainable and farmer-friendly food for the future, particularly in the context of climate change. Adi stated that the ASEAN-India Millet Festival provides an opportunity to promote the advantages of millets, including nutritional benefits, environmental sustainability, and economic development. The 'ASEAN-India Millets Festival', located at Kota Kasablanka Mall in South Jakarta, a popular shopping destination, seeks to develop a market for millets and related products among ASEAN members. The ASEAN bloc consists of Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, and Cambodia. Millets are capable of growing in dry regions with minimal resources and are resistant to climate variations. Consequently, they offer an ideal solution for countries aiming to enhance self-sufficiency and decrease dependence on imported grains. India spearheaded the UN General Assembly resolution declaring 2023 as the 'International Year of Millets', an initiative designed to address food security challenges. This year also aims to promote sustainable millet production and highlight their potential to create new market opportunities for both producers and consumers. The Indian Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is leading a delegation at the event, which includes representatives from Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), industry leaders, and other professionals. The Millet-centric exhibition includes participation from Millet-based FPOs, start-ups, and Indian chefs.  The exhibition also aims to encourage cooperation among ASEAN countries, celebrate cultural and culinary diversity, and promote sustainable millet practices for improved health outcomes. Five Indian FPOs—Citi Block FPC, Jewargi Taluka Millets FPC, Bhumitrajalalpur, Vaam Agro, and Lambasingi Tribal Products FPC—and two start-ups—Taru Naturals and Sattva Millets and Food Products (Mibbles)—are showcasing unique millet products such as millet cookies, namkeen, khakhra, and cakes. Ankit Patel, representing Vaam Agro, a spice company based in Ahmedabad, mentioned that they began producing millet-based products four months prior and have already achieved sales worth Rs 50 lakhs. 'We started with six millet products, including Dhokla and Khakhra, and the response has been excellent,' Patel said. Rizal Satria, based in Indonesia, noted that he started manufacturing millet-based products three years ago when public awareness was low. 'Now, more people are aware, and we anticipate consistent growth in our millet business,' he stated. A key highlight of the festival is the live cooking workshop, featuring celebrity chefs from India and Indonesia demonstrating the culinary versatility of millets.
translated_content: JAKAARTAA: Hindii Ayyaana Midhaan-guddaa guyyaa shan qabu Jakaartaa, Indoneeziyaa keessatti eegalte, kunis hubannoo midhaan-guddaa akka filannoo nyaataa itti fufiinsa qabuufi qonnaan-bulaaf mijaa'aa ta'etti dabaluufi. Ergamaan Indiyaa gara ASEAN (Waldaa Biyyoota Kibba Bahaa Eeshiyaa) fi Ministeerri Qonnaa fi Fayyaa Qonnaan Bulaa walta'uun 'Ayyaana Midhaan-guddaa ASEAN-Indiyaa', kan Onkoloolessa 22 jalqabe qopheessaa jiru. Wantoota ayyaanichaa keessaa inni guddaan agarsiisa Midhaan-guddaarratti xiyyeeffate kan Dhaabbatoota Oomishaa Qonnaan Bulaa (FPOs) kan midhaan-guddaarratti hundaa'an, jalqabbiiwwan, fi chefota Indiyaa agarsiisudha. Barri kun akkasumas oomishaa midhaan-guddaa itti fufiinsa qabu babal'isuufi dandeettii isaanii carraaqee gabaa haaraa itti fufiinsa qabu oomishitootaafi fayyadamtootaaf uumuuf qaban ibsuuf kaayyoo qaba. Ministeerri Qonnaa fi Fayyaa Qonnaan Bulaa Indiyaa gara ayyaanichaatti ergamaa hogganaa jira, kunis bakka buutota Dhaabbatoota Oomishaa Qonnaan Bulaa (FPOs), hoogganoota warshaa, fi ogeessota biroo of keessatti qabata. Agarsiisni Midhaan-guddaarratti xiyyeeffate hirmaannaa Dhaabbatoota Oomishaa Qonnaan Bulaa kan midhaan-guddaarratti hundaa'an, jalqabbiiwwan, fi chefota Indiyaa of keessatti qabata. Agarsiisichi akkasumas walta'iinsa biyyoota ASEAN gidduutti jajjabeessuuf, adda addummaa aadaa fi nyaataa kabajuuf, fi gochawwan midhaan-guddaa itti fufiinsa qaban fayyaa fooyya'aa argamsiisuuf babal'isuuf kaayyoo qaba. FPOs Indiyaa shan—Citi Block FPC, Jewargi Taluka Millets FPC, Bhumitrajalalpur, Vaam Agro, fi Lambasingi Tribal Products FPC—fi jalqabbiiwwan lama—Taru Naturals fi Sattva Millets and Food Products (Mibbles)—oomishaalee midhaan-guddaa addaa kan akka biskileetii midhaan-guddaa, naankiin, khakhra, fi keeki agarsiisaa jiru. 'Oomishaalee midhaan-guddaa ja'aan jalqabne, Dhoklaa fi Khakhraa dabalatee, deebiin argame gaarii ture,' jedhan Patel. article_content: Leading Labour figures yesterday demanded that Tony Blair face questioning over torture. As the call for a judge-led inquiry grew, Alan Johnson and Yvette Cooper urged that the former prime minister be questioned on Britain’s role in the barbaric treatment of prisoners by the US. This comes as the Daily Mail publishes a letter from more than 40 prominent figures, including politicians and authors, appealing for David Cameron to secure the release of a British father of four held for 13 years without trial in Guantanamo Bay. Scroll down for video. Former Prime Minister Tony Blair and the then Foreign Secretary Jack Straw are facing questions about what they knew regarding CIA torture. Shadow home secretary Miss Cooper also indicated she believed an investigation by a judge might be necessary to uncover the truth about torture. Her statement means the Labour front bench is close to supporting an inquiry that could be highly embarrassing for both Mr Blair and David Miliband – the brother of the party’s current leader. MPs stated that former foreign secretary Jack Straw – who has been interviewed as a ‘witness’ by detectives investigating the rendition of two Libyan dissidents – must also be held accountable. Last night, former Tory Attorney General Dominic Grieve supported the calls for a judge-led inquiry once the police investigations are concluded, saying it was needed to provide ‘finality’. And former shadow home secretary David Davis told Sky News that a judge must take charge. He said: ‘One must understand the sheer weight of pressure from the Establishment to try and prevent this sort of information from coming out, so I think this needs to be a judicial inquiry.’ At Westminster, the weekend was dominated by the continued fallout from last week’s Senate Intelligence Committee report, which detailed how detainees had been subjected to torture such as waterboarding. Mr Cameron continues to maintain the position that an inquiry by Parliament’s Intelligence and Security Committee is the best approach to determine the level of Britain’s involvement. In a publicity announcement, ISC chairman Sir Malcolm Rifkind yesterday said he had asked the Senate committee to reveal the redactions, requested by British security officials, which resulted in all mentions of MI5 and MI6 being removed from the 499-page report. Sir Malcolm Rifkind told the BBC's Andrew Marr Show this morning that he would seek to question former ministers regarding Britain's role or complicity in torture. Shadow home secretary Yvette Cooper said her 'instinct' was to call for a full judicial inquiry into UK torture. Former foreign secretary Jack Straw was questioned by police investigating the abductions of two Libyan dissidents who claim they were handed over to Colonel Muammar Gaddafi and tortured by his regime. Mr Straw was interviewed as a 'witness' by Scotland Yard amid claims the British government was complicit in the 'rendition' of the two men and their families. The dissidents, Abdel Hakim Belhadj and Sami al-Saadi, have accused Mr Straw of authorizing the operations in 2004. A decision on whether to bring any charges could be made in the new year. He also stated his committee would ask any former or serving minister with relevant information to give evidence – placing the spotlight firmly on Mr Blair, Mr Straw and Mr Miliband. Sir Malcolm added: ‘If they refuse to do so, that in itself would imply they have something to hide. If there is evidence they knew or were involved then of course they would be priority figures for our investigation. ‘If people deserve to be embarrassed it’s our job to embarrass them. We have a statutory obligation to carry out this task without fear or favour.’ However, he admitted that he had no way of compelling the Americans to hand over an uncensored copy of the report. He also conceded he could not say he was ‘confident’ of success. Home Secretary Theresa May will be questioned today by the Home Affairs Select Committee on the extent of her contact with the Senate committee and whether she personally lobbied for any redactions. ISC member George Howarth said it was right to seek details of redacted material but questioned why it should come from the US. He said the priority should be to seek answers directly from the Government and intelligence agencies. The Labour MP added: ‘It could take months and what we are asking for already exists in London.’ Miss Cooper said she doubted the ISC ‘have the capacity and the scope’ to conduct an inquiry, adding that her ‘instinct’ was that a judge-led process would still be required to ensure confidence. She told the BBC that Mr Blair and other former ministers had ‘always said that they would co-operate with all investigations and have said that they would be very keen to do so’. Former Prime Minister Tony Blair met the former Libyan leader Colonel Gaddafi at his desert base outside Sirte south of Tripoli in 2007. A Parliamentary committee has called on the US government to provide any evidence of British complicity in torture. Last week a US Senate report exposed the "brutal" treatment of al-Qaeda terror suspects following 9/11. Downing Street has admitted that some material was removed from the report at the UK's request, for national security reasons. But it said no redactions related to British involvement in the mistreatment of prisoners. The House of Commons Intelligence and Security Committee is conducting an inquiry into the treatment of detainees by British intelligence agencies in the decade following 9/11. Sir Malcolm Rifkind, who heads the intelligence committee, told the BBC's Andrew Marr Show it would request to see redacted material in the Senate's public report if it referenced the UK. He said that if British intelligence officials were present when people were being tortured then they were complicit in that torture. "That would be quite against all the standards of this country, it would be something that ought to be brought into the public domain," Sir Malcolm added. Miss Cooper added that it was important to get to the truth to ensure there was no ‘shadow of innuendo or allegations cast over the vital work that the [security] agencies rightly do to keep us all safe every day of the week’. Former home secretary Mr Johnson said Mr Straw and Mr Blair should appear before the committee. Asked on the Andrew Marr show if they should give evidence, he said: ‘Yes, absolutely, yes.’ Former deputy prime minister Lord Prescott also called for a judicial inquiry. He wrote in his Sunday Mirror column: ‘We must have a transparent system that reflects our values of fair play and justice, not one that turns a blind eye and deaf ear to claims of the abduction and torture of innocent people.’ Tory Defence Secretary Michael Fallon called for Mr Straw and Mr Blair to reveal what they knew about the CIA’s torture and rendition programme when they were in office. He said: ‘Obviously it’s for them, it’s for former ministers to account for the relationship then. I hope they will co-operate with any parliamentary inquiry.’ Civil liberties groups and campaigning MPs accuse Britain of repeatedly turning a blind eye to torture during Mr Blair’s ‘war on terror’ – when he worked closely with the Bush administration. There are allegations that British agents were present when torture took place and that the UK assisted with rendition flights. Yesterday, one of the two psychologists who were paid to run the interrogation programme by the CIA insisted UK agents were at torture sites. Dr James Mitchell, who devised the brutal ‘enhanced interrogation’ programmes, said: ‘I’d see their special operations people at the sites I would visit.’ Lib Dem Business Secretary Vince Cable said the ISC and police investigations into the Libyan renditions should be allowed to ‘run their course’. He added: ‘If at the end of it, it doesn’t appear that the truth is emerging, that people imagine there is some kind of cover-up, then of course a judge-led inquiry is the right way to proceed.’ Isabella Sankey of human rights group Liberty said: ‘Until our Government sets up a transparent, judicial inquiry, cover-up and official impunity will persist.’

Ibsi isheen kennite kun, kutaan fuulduraa Leebaralootaa qorannoo qaanii guddaa Mr Blair fi David Miliband – obboleessa hoogganaa paartii amma jiruu – irratti geessisuu danda’u deeggaruuf dhiyaataa jiraachuu isaa agarsiisa. Miseensonni Mana Marii Bakka Bu’ootaa Ministirri Dhimma Alaa duraanii Jack Straw – kanneen dhimma lammiilee Liibiyaa lama biyya biraatti dabarsuu fi dararuu qoratan poolisii ‘ragaa baatuu’ ta’uun gaafataman – itti gaafatamuu qabu jedhaniiru. Kaleessa galgala, Abukaatoonni Seeraa Toorii duraanii Dominic Grieve erga qorannoowwan poolisii xumuraman booda waamicha qorannoo abbaa seeraa durfamuuf deeggaranii, kun ‘dhuma’ akka fiduuf barbaachisaa dha jedhaniiru. Haati manaa ministira dhimma keessaa duraanii David Davis Sky Newsitti abbaan seeraa itti gaafatamummaa fudhachuu qaba jedhaniiru. Inni akkas jedhe: ‘Dhiibbaan qaama aangoo irraa dhufu kun baay’ee ulfaataa ta’uu isaa hubachuun barbaachisaa dha, dhimmoonni akkanaa akka hin baaneef yaalii godhu, kanaafuu kun qorannoo abbaa seeraa durfamu barbaada natti fakkaata.’ Westminsteritti, torbee dhumaa dhimma gabaasa Koree Odeeffannoo Senetii torbee darbee irraa dhufeen kan mo’amee ture, kunis hidhamtoonni reebicha akka bishaaniin reebuun kanneen akka gochaatti akka saaxilaman ibsa. Mr Cameron ammas qorannoon Koree Odeeffannoo fi Nageenya Mana Marii Bakka Bu’ootaa gaheen Britaniyaa keessatti qabdu hammam akka ta’e baruuf mala gaarii ta’uu isaa irratti cichaa jira. Beeksisa ummataaf oolu keessatti, dura taa’aan ISC Sir Malcolm Rifkind kaleessa koree Senetii gaaffii sirreeffamaa, kanneen hooggantoota nageenyaa Britaniyaan gaafataman, kanneen maqaan MI5 fi MI6 gabaasa fuula 499 qabu irraa guutummaatti akka haqamu godhan akka ifa godhu gaafataniiru. Sir Malcolm Rifkind BBC's Andrew Marr Show har’a ganama irratti gaheen Britaniyaa ykn hirmaannaan isheen reebicha keessatti qabdu ilaalchisee ministeerota duraanii gaafachuuf akka yaalan dubbataniiru. Haati manaa ministira dhimma keessaa Yvette Cooper ‘miirri’ ishee qorannoo abbaa seeraa guutuu reebicha UK keessatti raawwatameef waamicha gochuu akka ta’e dubbataniiru. Ministirri dhimma alaa duraanii Jack Straw poolisiin dhimma butuutaa lammiilee Liibiyaa lama kanneen Koloneel Mu’ammar Gaddafiitti dabarsamanii dararamaniiru jedhan qoratan gaafataniiru. Mr Straw Scotland Yardiin ‘ragaa baatuu’ ta’uun gaafatameera, kunis mootummaan Britaniyaa ‘birootti dabarsuu’ dhiirotaa lamaanii fi maatii isaaniitti hirmaachaa ture jedhamee himatamaa jira. Lammiileen Liibiyaa lama, Abdel Hakim Belhadj fi Sami al-Saadi, Mr Straw hojiiwwan bara 2004tti raawwataman akka mirkaneessan himataniiru. Murtiin himanni kamiyyuu dhihaachuu danda’uuf bara haaraa keessatti kennamuu danda’a. Akkasumas koreen isaa ministeera duraanii ykn tajaajila irra jiran kanneen odeeffannoo barbaachisaa qaban ragaa akka kennan gaafachuu isaa ibseera – kunis xiyyeeffannoo Mr Blair, Mr Straw fi Mr Miliband irratti akka xiyyeeffatu godha. Sir Malcolm itti dabaluun: ‘Yoo kana gochuu didan, kun mataa isaa keessatti wanti dhoksuu qaban jiraachuu isaa agarsiisa. Ragaan isaan beekan ykn keessatti hirmaatan yoo jiraate yeroo sana isaan akka namoota dursa kennamuuf qorannoo keenyaaf ta’uufii isaanii hin oolamu. ‘Yoo namoonni qaana’uu qaban ta’e qaaneessuun hojii keenya. Hojii kana sodaafii loogii malee raawwachuuf dirqama seeraa qabna.’ Haa ta’u malee, Ameerikaan gabaasa hin sirreeffamne akka isaaniif kennan dirqisiisuuf karaa hin qabne akka qaban amaniiru. Akkasumas milkaa’ina isaatti ‘amantaa’ qaba jedhee dubbachuu akka hin dandeenye amaniiru. Haati manaa ministira dhimma keessaa Theresa May har’a Koree Filannoo Dhimma Keessaa Mana Marii Bakka Bu’ootaan dhimma hariiroo isheen koree Senetii waliin qabduu fi sirreeffamoota kamiyyuu mataa isheen dhiibbaa gootetti hangam akka gaafatamtuuf gaafatamuuf jirti. Miseensi ISC George Howarth odeeffannoo sirreeffamee jiru bal’inaan barbaaduun sirrii ta’uu isaa dubbatan, garuu maaliif Ameerikaa irraa dhufuu qaba jedhanii gaafataniiru. Inni dursa kan kennamuuf mootummaadhaanii fi dhaabbilee nageenyaa irraa kallattiin deebii barbaaduu akka ta’uu qabu dubbataniiru. Hayyuun Mana Marii Bakka Bu’ootaa Leebaralootaa itti dabaluun: ‘Ji’oota fudhachuu danda’a, wanti nuti gaafachaa jirru amma iyyuu Landan keessa jira.’ Itti Aantuun Cooper ISC ‘dandeettii fi bal’ina’ qorannoo gaggeessuuf akka hin qabne shakkii qabaachuu ishee dubbatte, itti dabaluunis ‘miirri’ ishee adeemsi abbaa seeraa durfamu ammas amantaa mirkaneessuuf barbaachisaa ta’uu isaa dubbatte. Isheen BBCtti Mr Blair fi ministeeronni duraanii biroo ‘qorannoowwan hundaaf walii galuu fi kana gochuuf baay’ee hawwaa akka ta’an yeroo hundumaa dubbataniiru’ jettee himte. Muummichi Ministeeraa duraanii Tony Blair bara 2007tti hoogganaa Liibiyaa duraanii Koloneel Gaddafi buufata isaa gammoojjii keessatti Sirte kibba Tripoli keessatti wal arganii turan. Koreen Mana Marii Bakka Bu’ootaa mootummaa US ragaa hirmaannaa Britaniyaa reebicha keessatti qabdu kamiyyuu akka dhiheessu gaafataniiru. Torbee darbee gabaasni Senetii US ‘gocha suukaneessaa’ shakkamtoota al-Qaeda 9/11 booda raawwatame saaxileera. Downing Street odeeffannoon tokko tokko gabaasa irraa gaaffii UKtiin, sababoota nageenya biyyaatiif, akka haqame amaniiru. Garuu sirreeffamoonni hirmaannaa Britaniyaa dhimma hidhamtoota dararuu keessatti qabdu ilaalchisee akka hin jirre dubbataniiru. Koreen Odeeffannoo fi Nageenya Mana Marii Bakka Bu’ootaa qorannoo dhimma hidhamtoota dhaabbilee odeeffannoo Britaniyaan waggoota 9/11 booda raawwatamanii gaggeessaa jira. Sir Malcolm Rifkind, kanneen koree odeeffannoo hogganan, BBC's Andrew Marr Showtti gabaasa Senetii ummataaf dhihaate keessatti odeeffannoo sirreeffamee jiru arguu akka gaafatan yoo UK ilaalchisee ibsamee dubbataniiru. Hooggantoonni odeeffannoo Britaniyaa yeroo namoonni dararamaa turan bakka sana yoo argaman, yeroo sana isaan reebicha sana keessatti hirmaachaa turan jechuudha jedhaniiru. “Kun sadarkaa biyya kanaa hundumaa faallaadha, kun wanta ummataaf ifa gochuun barbaachisu dha,” Sir Malcolm itti dabaluun dubbataniiru. Itti Aantuun Cooper dhugaa bira gahuun baay’ee barbaachisaa akka ta’e, kunis ‘gaaddidduu innuendo ykn himannaa hojii murteessaa dhaabbileen [nageenyaa] sirriitti guyyaa guyyaatti nu hundaaf nageenya keenya eeguuf hojjetan irratti hin buufneef’ jechuudhaan dubbataniiru. Ministirri dhimma keessaa duraanii Mr Johnson Mr Straw fi Mr Blair koree fuulduratti dhihaachuu qabu jedhaniiru. Andrew Marr show irratti ragaa kennuu qabu yoo gaafataman: ‘Eeyyee, sirritti, eeyyee’ jedhaniiru. Muummichi ministeeraa duraanii Itti Aantuu Lord Prescottis qorannoo abbaa seeraa durfamuuf waamicha godhaniiru. Inni barruu isaa Sunday Mirror keessatti akkas jedhee barreesseera: ‘Sirni iftoomina qabu kan safuufi haqaa keenya agarsiisu qabaachuu qabna, isa ija dunuunfatee fi gurra duuchee himannaa butuutaa fi dararuu namoota yakka hin qabnee hin fudhanne.’ Ministirri Ittisaa Toorii Michael Fallon Mr Straw fi Mr Blair dhimma reebichaa CIA fi biyya biraatti dabarsuu ilaalchisee wanta beekan yeroo hojii irra turan akka ifa godhan waamicha godhaniiru. Akkas jedhan: ‘Ifatti isaanumaaf, ministeerota duraaniif hariiroo yeroo sanaa ibsuufii dha. Qorannoo Mana Marii Bakka Bu’ootaa kamiyyuu waliin akka walii galan nan abdaddha.’ Dhaabbileen bilisummaa hawaasaa fi miseensonni Mana Marii Bakka Bu’ootaa duula gaggeessan Britaniyaan yeroo ‘waraana shororkeessaa’ Mr Blair – yeroo inni bulchiinsa Bush waliin walitti dhufeenya cimaa qabu hojjetetti – yeroo baay’ee ija dunuunfattee reebicha akka ilaaltu himatu. Himannaan hooggantoonni Britaniyaa yeroo reebichi raawwatamaa ture bakka sana akka argamanii fi UK imala biyya biraatti dabarsuu keessatti akka gargaarte jira. Kaleessa, hayyoota xiinqaa lamaan keessaa tokko kanneen sagantaa gaafannoo CIAtiin gaggeeffamuuf kaffaltii kennamuu kanneen UK bakka reebichaa irratti argamu jedhanii cimsanii dubbataniiru. Doktar James Mitchell, kanneen sagantaawwan ‘gaafannoo cimaa’ suukaneessaa qopheessan, akkas jedhaniiru: ‘Namoota hojii addaa isaanii bakka ani daawwadhutti nan arga ture.’ Haati manaa ministira dhimma daldalaa Lib Dem Vince Cable qorannoowwan ISC fi poolisii dhimma biyya biraatti dabarsuu Liibiyaa ilaalchisee ‘adeemsa isaanii akka xumuran’ hayyamamuu qaba jedhaniiru. Itti dabaluunis: ‘Dhuma irratti, dhugaan ba’aa akka hin jirre yoo mul’ate, namoonni haguuggii tokko jira jedhanii yoo yaadan, yeroo sana qorannoon abbaa seeraa durfamu karaa sirrii ta’uu isaa hin oolamu.’ Isabella Sankey kan garee mirga namoomaa Liberty akkas jette: ‘Hanga Mootummaan keenya qorannoo iftoomina qabu, abbaa seeraa durfamu hin dhaabneetti, haguuggiin fi dhimmoonni seeraan alaa hojjetaman itti fufu.’

To guarantee topping their group and reaching the last 16, Dortmund must now beat Anderlecht in their last game.  Their strong European form contrasts sharply with their poor domestic league position, where Klopp's team is third from bottom in the Bundesliga.  Dortmund players acknowledged their fans after the Arsenal match as home fans watched. Following their Champions League defeat, Dortmund players went to their supporters.  Manager Jurgen Klopp spoke with Adrian Ramos after the game. Alexis Sanchez scored Arsenal's second goal. article_content: Los Angeles (CNN) -- Lawyers for Dr. Conrad Murray, the doctor convicted in pop star Michael Jackson's death, are warning that he is suffering potentially life-threatening and permanent injuries after nearly a year in a small jail cell. Due to his notoriety, Dr. Murray is housed in a high-security section of the Los Angeles County jail. This isolation, intended for his protection, separates him from the general population and significantly limits his access to exercise. In a letter to Los Angeles County Sheriff Lee Baca on Wednesday, lawyers Valerie Wass and Michael Flanagan argued, 'Death or injury from another prisoner is no worse than a slow death caused by poor circulation and muscle atrophy resulting from the inhumane confinement of a large man in a tiny space.' Dr. Murray has been jailed since November 7, 2011, following his conviction for involuntary manslaughter in Jackson's death. The letter states that Murray, who is 6 feet 5 inches tall, is confined to a 5-foot-by-7-foot cell. The lawyers drew a comparison, stating, 'If a dog were kept in a space only slightly larger than its length for an extended period, it would likely be considered animal cruelty and could lead to prosecution.' The sheriff's office did not immediately respond to CNN's requests for comment. Wass, who is overseeing the appeal of Murray's conviction, told CNN on Thursday that his jail conditions are 'the equivalent of a large individual flying coach in a middle seat for a year.' Murray was hospitalized on Sunday night for treatment of what his lawyer described as 'marked venous stasis of his lower extremities' and 'right shoulder pain and severe loss of motion.' Flanagan's letter suggested that the sheriff has 'alternatives available to protect society and punish offenders that would not likely result in permanent injury or death to an inmate.' California law allows Sheriff Baca, at his discretion, to release Murray to monitored home confinement. Otherwise, he is expected to remain in jail for another year. Murray was found guilty of causing Jackson's death on June 25, 2009, by administering a fatal dose of sedatives and propofol, a surgical anesthetic, in an attempt to treat the singer's insomnia, according to his police statement. He received the maximum sentence of four years in prison but is eligible for parole after serving half of it. A California law aimed at reducing state prison overcrowding resulted in Murray being held in the county jail. His lawyers wrote that his cell is so small that Murray has 'no opportunity for physical movement throughout the day.' 'The only exercise Dr. Murray gets is on most Monday evenings when he is transferred in chains to an 8-by-8 cage on the roof,' they added. In a phone call to a friend on Monday, published Wednesday by TMZ, Murray expressed fear that his illness could be permanent. 'I may never be able to wear a boot again,' he said. His lawyer wrote to the sheriff that 'the venous stasis gives rise to a high risk for deep vein thrombosis and/or migrating pulmonary embolism. This condition may have become chronic and permanent, requiring lifelong medication and treatment.' Murray's lawyers also noted a dramatic change in his physical appearance since his incarceration. 'A comparison of earlier booking photos and bio-statistics of Dr. Murray to his current condition and appearance would be shocking to those unfamiliar with him. To those who have known him over the last year, the toll on his health is unimaginable,' they wrote. The letter concluded, 'Keeping a human in such conditions would at least result in civil liability for negligent confinement causing a debilitating medical condition.' They urged the sheriff, 'Please consider this letter as notice of Dr. Murray's life-threatening condition. Correcting this intolerable situation is extremely important.' Adabbiin isaa waggaa afurii kan guddinaa ta'eef, garuu adabbii isaa walakkaa erga xumureen booda bilisa ba'uuf gahee dha. Abukaatoonni isaa akka barreessanitti mana hidhaa isaa baay'ee xiqqaa waan ta'eef Marrii 'guutuu guyyaa sochii qaamaa gochuuf carraa hin qabu.' 'Shaakala qaamaa Doktar Marrii argatu kan biraa irra caalaa galgala Wiixataa yeroo inni mana hidhaa qaamaa keessaa gara mana hidhaa meetira 2.4 x meetira 2.4 ta'etti hidhaan funyoo sibiilaatiin hidhamee geeffamu qofa.' jedhaniiru. Bilbilaan gaafa Wiixataa hiriyyaa tokkoof bilbilame, kan gaafa Roobii TMZ maxxanseen, Marrii dhukkubni isaa kan yeroo hundumaaf turuu danda'u sodaachaa akka jiru ibseera. 'Deebitee kophee uffachuu hin danda'u ta'a,' jedhe. Abukaatoonni isaa shariifiif akka barreessanitti 'dhiigni hidda dhiigaa sirnaan hin naanna'uu kun balaa guddaa dhiiga hidda dhiigaa gadi fagoo keessatti kuufamuufi/ykn dhiiga gara sombaatti godaanuu danda'uuf ni kenna. Haalli kun gara haala yeroo dheeraatti jijjiiramuutti kan jijjiiramee fi kan yeroo hundumaaf ta'ee fi qorichaafi yaala jireenya guutuu barbaaduu danda'a.' Abukaatoonni Marrii jijjiirama guddinaa mul'ataa ta'e haala qaamaa isaa irratti yeroo inni mana hidhaatti galefii kaasee akka hubatan ibsaniiru. 'Haala qaamaa fi bifa Doktar Marrii yeroo ammaatiin wal bira qabuun suuraa fi biyo-istaatiiksii Doktar Marrii kan duraa yoo ilaalan namoota isa hin beekneef kan nama ajaa'ibsiisu ta'a. Namoota waggaa darbe keessa isa beekanitti, miidhaan fayyaa isaa irra ga'e hin yaadamu,' jedhaniiru. article_content: Kyle Dube, 20, pleaded not guilty on Wednesday to charges of murder and kidnapping. He is accused of creating a fake Facebook profile to lure 15-year-old Nichole Cable to her death. During his arraignment at the Penobscot Judicial Center, Dube’s defense lawyer, Stephen Smith, requested a psychological evaluation to determine if Dube is competent to stand trial. The court appearance was brief, and Dube was returned to jail afterward. Nichole Cable’s mother attended, wearing a yellow T-shirt with her daughter’s picture and holding a stuffed teddy bear. Facebook records identified Dube, at his parents’ Orono home, as the owner of the fake account. Dube’s girlfriend, Sarah Mersinger, told detectives Dube disclosed the location of Nichole’s body. Dube’s brother, Dustin Dube, also provided information to the police.
